RPR-2026-10.why: Carla is Agnes's daughter, not a parent of a minor or disabled adult in her household nor her spouse, so she files every year when asked (20 CFR 404.2065; the 2018 Act's four exemptions). For October 2025 to September 2026: $20,976 received (three months at $1,712, nine at $1,760); $18,600 on food and housing (Oakview's board and care, twelve months at $1,550); $1,011 on everything else (pharmacy, salon, clothing, batteries, eyeglasses, shoes); and $3,246.20 in savings at the period's end, last year's $1,840 with the $1,365 swept in and $41.20 of interest. October 2026's spending belongs to next year. Counted as an item at $0: it is the chore's minutes, not money

traps.RPR-2026-10: An adult child is not among the payees the 2018 Act exempts (a parent or guardian of a minor in the same household, a parent of a disabled adult in the same household, a spouse): claiming it is a false statement signed under penalty of perjury
